requirement:
A paragraph has no declared name. Each prose paragraph has an anonymous
`paragraph` node under its nearest
enclosing outline container. This includes paragraphs before the first heading
and inside list items, quotations, and directive bodies. Their selectors follow
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Heading text and literal
code-block contents create no paragraph nodes. Syntax that has no outline node
is transparent when finding the enclosing container.
rationale:
The three marked tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/markdown_tests.rs` cover every obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.paragraphs`. I did not read the implementation beyond a search snippet. Where I mention a root section, that is my inference from the test assertions about node index 1.

- **Anonymous `paragraph` node under the nearest enclosing container.**
  - `paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges` asserts the full node list from `kinds(&outline)`. A paragraph under the `# Authentication` section has its parent set to that section. Paragraphs inside the `::::{note}` and nested `:::{tip}` directive bodies have the directive `block` as parent.
  - Every node resolves from its selector back to its own index. Non-section nodes use an anonymous `paragraph@<12-char hash>` segment. This checks that the paragraph is anonymous and follows the selector grammar in `requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
- **Paragraphs before the first heading, in list items and in quotations.**
  - `paragraphs_in_transparent_lists_and_quotes_are_selectable` uses the source "Before heading", "- List paragraph.", "> Quoted paragraph.", a setext `Title`, then "After heading".
  - It asserts exactly four paragraph nodes with their expected start lines.
  - The first three have a section node (index 1, which I read as the root or preamble section) as parent. They are not parented to a list or quote node, so lists and quotes are transparent.
  - The paragraph after the heading has `section[Title]` as parent.
- **Paragraphs in directive bodies.** The nested-directive test covers these, including nesting two levels deep, with parent and line-range assertions.
- **Heading text creates no paragraph.** Both tests assert the exact node lists or paragraph counts. Neither the ATX heading nor the setext `Title` heading produces a paragraph.
- **Literal code-block contents create no paragraph.** The fenced `text` block containing `hi` appears only as a `block` node, and the exact node list has no paragraph child for it.
- **Selectors, including duplicates.**
  - `anonymous_identities_survive_reflow_and_sibling_edits_and_number_duplicates` checks that paragraph selectors stay stable under reflow and under edits to sibling content.
  - It also checks that duplicate paragraphs ("Same." twice) get `#1` and `#2` suffixes.

The assertions are exact (fixed parents, counts and ranges), so a wrong parent, an extra paragraph or a missing paragraph would fail them. Two cases are not tested: indented, as opposed to fenced, code blocks, and a list or quote nested inside a directive. Both fall under the same transparency and parent-selection logic as the tested cases, so I do not count them as gaps. There are no `{fixme}` acknowledgments.
